newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila's PHIBOR edge up at short end of the curve.
newsitem.headline: Manila's PHIBOR edge up at short end of the curve.

text.p: The Philippine interbank offered rates (PHIBOR) were firmer at the short end of the curve, while the three and six-month maturities remained unchanged, traders said on Monday.

A trader said the rising spot rates had prompted many banks to adjust their swap rates higher. Major banks have parked their excess funds in special Central Bank bills, siphoning off liquidity for short-term borrowings.
He added banks were still cautious in their medium term outlook awaiting the results of the Treasury bill auction later in the day.
PHIBOR are average rates for foreign exchange forward rates quoted by 20 banks operating in the country.
